## Overview Registers `ConnexConnector`, a pull-based P/D connector whose prefill-side KV stays available as a renewable hold, so a request whose decode instance dies can be resumed on another decode instance without a second prefill. The implementation ships in the optional [`connex-ai`](https://github.com/HeterInfra/connex) package (same pattern as `LMCacheConnectorV1`); vLLM gains no dependency and no code path changes for other connectors. **Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs/issues for `connex`, P/D fault tolerance and elastic P/D connectors. #55151 ("[wip] support PD seperate mode for fault-tolerance", no description or code yet) targets fault tolerance in vLLM's own P/D path; this PR does not touch that path and adds an external connector with request-level resume. #59330 (stop P/D transfers at N-1) changes NIXL/Mooncake semantics for sliding-window models; ConnexConnector currently supports full-attention models only and follows the current N-token load. ## Claims - New `kv_connector="ConnexConnector"`: decode pulls prompt KV with one-sided RDMA reads (connex-rs over UCX with GPUDirect RDMA, or Mooncake Transfer Engine). - Killing a decode instance mid-run loses no requests: affected requests resume elsewhere by re-pulling the held KV (0 extra prefills, 0 tokens off the argmax). - Steady-state TTFT/TPOT/throughput on par with `NixlConnector` on the same setup. - A prefill instance dying during a transfer fails only the affected loads (under `kv_load_failure_policy`). ## Validation ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_connex_connector.py -v # needs connex-ai, otherwise skipped pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py pre-commit run --files ``` On this branch (main d0d681e4) with current connex-ai: `test_connex_connector.py` 2 passed, `test_config.py` 17 passed, pre-commit on changed files passes. connex-ai's own suite covers the connector and router (CPU, fake engines) and the transfer core. **CI coverage gap:** the new tests `importorskip` connex-ai, which is not installed in vLLM CI, so CI will skip them; the validation above was run outside CI. End-to-end runs were done on vLLM 0.32.0 (not re-run on d0d681e4): 4x A40 on one host, ConnectX HDR, GPUDirect RDMA, Llama-3-8B, Connex PD router, prefill and decode on different GPUs. - **Correctness**, 1P1D, 48 prompts x 128 greedy tokens, teacher-forced against a non-disaggregated instance: 0 of 6,144 generated tokens off the argmax (> 0.5 nats) at concurrency 1 and 8. Exact-match differences (20 and 15 of 48) are at the level of the non-disaggregated instance against itself at different batch sizes (18 of 48). - **Failures** (240 requests, QPS 2, 1024-token prompts, 256 output tokens): - kill one of two decode instances: 240/240 complete, 9 resumed, all by re-pulling held KV (0 extra prefills), 0 off argmax, longest kill-to-next-token stall 0.63 s (3 runs, same outcome); - 2P2D, kill one decode and one prefill: 240/240, 11 resumes (11 re-pulls), 0 off argmax; - prefill killed while a transfer was pending (fault-injected, 3 runs): decode failed the load, router re-prefilled on the other prefill instance, all complete; - scaling a pool up and draining an instance under load: 240/240 complete.
Throughput/latency vs NixlConnector (1024-token prompts, 128 output tokens, same router and hosts) | connector | load | TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) | TPOT p50 / p99 (ms) | tok/s | |---|---|---|---|---| | ConnexConnector | QPS 1 | 354 / 537 | 31 / 33 | 128 | | NixlConnector | QPS 1 | 352 / 594 | 31 / 33 | 128 | | ConnexConnector | QPS 4 | 471 / 1003 | 36 / 38 | 459 | | NixlConnector | QPS 4 | 456 / 996 | 36 / 38 | 459 | | ConnexConnector | QPS 6 | 734 / 2090 | 38 / 40 | 694 | | NixlConnector | QPS 6 | 711 / 2018 | 38 / 40 | 694 | | ConnexConnector | 32 clients | 625 / 4939 | 38 / 38 | 639 | | NixlConnector | 32 clients | 573 / 4751 | 38 / 38 | 646 |
## Details Existing P/D connectors free the prefill blocks as soon as decode has read them, so once decoding starts the prompt KV exists in one place. If the decode instance dies (crash, preemption, spot scale-down), every in-flight request must be prefilled again or errors out. ConnexConnector makes the prefill-side copy a hold: a lease named by a transfer id, renewed by every pull, released by the decode instance when the request finishes or dropped after `retain_s` (default 60 s). `release: after_pull` frees blocks after the first read like other connectors. To resume, a router resends the same `kv_transfer_params` with the prompt plus the k generated tokens; the new decode instance async-loads `remote_num_tokens` and computes the k tokens locally. Instances can register their P/D role with the Connex front-router so instances can be added or removed at run time. Request flow: 1. Prefill instance (`kv_producer`) runs the prompt; on finish the scheduler keeps the blocks and returns `transfer_id`, `remote_ctrl`, `remote_num_tokens`. 2. Decode instance (`kv_consumer`) schedules the request as `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and pulls the blocks with one-sided reads. 3. Decode generates; on finish it sends a release, and the prefill worker reports the transfer done so the blocks are freed. 4. If decode dies before step 3, the router resends to another decode instance, which repeats step 2 against the still-held blocks. Changes: `v1/connex_connector.py` (lazy re-export with install hint), registration in `factory.py`, `docs/features/connex_connector_usage.md` plus an entry in `disagg_prefill.md`, and scheduler-level tests through the real `Scheduler`. Limitations: full-attention KV only; equal TP and block size on both sides. Developed with AI coding assistance; all changes were reviewed and tested by the author. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

### 🟡 Changes recommended The delegated adapter can report receive completion for a running cached-prefix request, triggering a scheduler assertion during resume.
4 open issues - [Suppress empty receive completions for cached-prefix pulls](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63804#discussion_r4380814752) · New - [Document that backend auto-selection requires leaving backend unset](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63804#discussion_r4380814840) · New - [Qualify no-reprefill recovery claim by API and resume mode](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63804#discussion_r4380814887) · New - [Assign distinct GPUs to prefill and decode servers](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63804#discussion_r4380814938) · New
What changed in this PR Adds optional ConnexConnector integration for prefill/decode disaggregation, using retained prefill KV to support recovery from decode-instance failures without changing other connectors. **Changes:** - Registers the connector through a lazy wrapper around `connex-ai`, with installation guidance. - Adds scheduler-level tests for KV retention, asynchronous loading, and release. - Documents setup, configuration, and supported deployment constraints. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `vllm/​distributed/​kv_transfer/​kv_connector/​v1/​connex_connector.py` | Re-exports the optional connector with an installation error message. | | `vllm/​distributed/​kv_transfer/​kv_connector/​factory.py` | Registers `ConnexConnector` for lazy loading. | | `tests/​v1/​kv_connector/​unit/​test_connex_connector.py` | Tests scheduler handoff and release when `connex-ai` is installed. | | `docs/​features/​disagg_prefill.md` | Adds Connex to the connector list. | | `docs/​features/​connex_connector_usage.md` | Documents installation, deployment, configuration, and limitations. |
Review effort: Balanced

The delegated adapter can crash the scheduler when a resumed request already has the remote prefix cached locally (e.g. 32 cached tokens, `remote_num_tokens=32`, and a longer resumed prompt). It returns `(0, False)` but still queues an empty pull in `update_state_after_alloc`, then reports its completion through `finished_recving`. The request is RUNNING, so `Scheduler._update_from_kv_xfer_finished` hits its finished-status assertion. Please fix the adapter to suppress receive completions for acquire-only pulls before exposing it here, and add a scheduler regression for this case.

@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+# ConnexConnector Usage Guide
+
+`ConnexConnector` moves KV cache blocks from prefill to decode instances with
+[Connex](https://github.com/HeterInfra/connex), a communication library whose
+endpoints keep a stable logical identity while instances join, leave and fail.
+The connector itself is provided by the `connex-ai` package; vLLM only
+registers it.
+
+What it adds over a plain P/D transfer:
+
+- **Pull with a renewable hold.** The decode instance reads the prompt KV with
+  one-sided RDMA reads (connex-rs over UCX with GPUDirect RDMA, or Mooncake
+  Transfer Engine). The prefill instance keeps the blocks under a transfer id
+  until the decode instance releases them (or a lease expires), so if the
+  decode instance fails mid-generation, the request can be resumed on another
+  decode instance that pulls the same KV again instead of re-running prefill.
+- **Failure reporting per request.** A prefill instance that dies during a
+  transfer fails only the affected requests (load errors, handled by
+  `kv_load_failure_policy`), detected within milliseconds by connex-rs.
+- **Pool membership.** Instances can register their role in a Connex
+  front-router, which the Connex PD router (`connex.serving.pd_router`) uses
+  to add and remove prefill and decode instances at run time.
+
+## Installation
+
+```bash
+pip install "connex-ai[rs]"        # connex-rs data plane (RDMA hosts)
+# or
+pip install "connex-ai[mooncake]"  # Mooncake Transfer Engine data plane
+```
+
+## Usage
+
+Prefill instance:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B --port 8100 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"ConnexConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"ctrl_port":17100}}'
+```
+
+Decode instance:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B --port 8200 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"ConnexConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"}'
+```
+
+Router (follows the same `kv_transfer_params` protocol as the NIXL proxy
+example: prefill with `do_remote_decode`, then decode with the returned
+parameters; it also resumes requests whose decode instance fails):
+
+```bash
+python -m connex.serving.pd_router --port 8000 \
+    --prefill http://127.0.0.1:8100 --decode http://127.0.0.1:8200
+```
+
+## Configuration
+
+`kv_connector_extra_config` keys:
+
+| key | default | meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `backend` | `auto` | `connex-rs`, `mooncake` or `auto` |

nodes.body: Please qualify the no-reprefill recovery claim by API and resume mode. In Connex's `PDResumer.build()`, a retry after tokens have been emitted discards the saved KV parameters unless token-ID resume is active on a non-chat request, so chat and text-based resume run prefill again even while the hold exists. Document this restriction for users relying on KV reuse during failover.

nodes.body: The router example uses loopback addresses, but these two server commands select the same default GPU when run on one host. The connex-rs data plane explicitly rejects transfers when prefill and decode share a GPU, so this quickstart cannot transfer KV as written (and the second server may run out of memory first). Assign distinct GPUs to the two roles, for example GPU 0 for prefill and GPU 1 for decode.

nodes.body: Confirmed: for a resumed request whose remote prefix is fully cached locally, `get_num_new_matched_tokens` returns `(0, False)`, the request runs, and the worker still reported the hold-acquiring pull in `finished_recving`, which hits the assertion in `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished`. Fixed in connex-ai: such a pull is now marked acquire-only (`_Pull.report=False` when `num_external_tokens == 0`) and the worker drops its completion instead of reporting it (a failed acquire is only logged; nothing local depends on it). connex-ai has a worker-level test for it. In this PR, 8e796c18 adds `test_resume_with_locally_cached_remote_prefix_runs_without_load`: it fills the local prefix cache, resumes a request whose `remote_num_tokens` equals the cached prefix, and checks that the request runs immediately, that its pull is acquire-only with no local blocks, and that the next steps proceed without a receive report. It skips on connex-ai releases that do not have this fix.

## Overview Registers `ConnexConnector`, a pull-based P/D connector whose prefill-side KV stays available as a renewable hold, so a request whose decode instance dies can be resumed on another decode instance without a second prefill. The implementation ships in the optional [`connex-ai`](https://github.com/HeterInfra/connex) package (same pattern as `LMCacheConnectorV1`); vLLM gains no dependency and no code path changes for other connectors. **Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs/issues for `connex`, P/D fault tolerance and elastic P/D connectors. #55151 ("[wip] support PD seperate mode for fault-tolerance", no description or code yet) targets fault tolerance in vLLM's own P/D path; this PR does not touch that path and adds an external connector with request-level resume. #59330 (stop P/D transfers at N-1) changes NIXL/Mooncake semantics for sliding-window models; ConnexConnector currently supports full-attention models only and follows the current N-token load. ## Claims - New `kv_connector="ConnexConnector"`: decode pulls prompt KV with one-sided RDMA reads (connex-rs over UCX with GPUDirect RDMA, or Mooncake Transfer Engine). - Killing a decode instance mid-run loses no requests: affected requests resume elsewhere by re-pulling the held KV (0 extra prefills, 0 tokens off the argmax). - Steady-state TTFT/TPOT/throughput on par with `NixlConnector` on the same setup. - A prefill instance dying during a transfer fails only the affected loads (under `kv_load_failure_policy`). ## Validation ```bash pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_connex_connector.py -v # needs connex-ai, otherwise skipped pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_config.py pre-commit run --files ``` On this branch (main d0d681e4) with current connex-ai: `test_connex_connector.py` 2 passed, `test_config.py` 17 passed, pre-commit on changed files passes. connex-ai's own suite covers the connector and router (CPU, fake engines) and the transfer core. **CI coverage gap:** the new tests `importorskip` connex-ai, which is not installed in vLLM CI, so CI will skip them; the validation above was run outside CI. End-to-end runs were done on vLLM 0.32.0 (not re-run on d0d681e4): 4x A40 on one host, ConnectX HDR, GPUDirect RDMA, Llama-3-8B, Connex PD router, prefill and decode on different GPUs. - **Correctness**, 1P1D, 48 prompts x 128 greedy tokens, teacher-forced against a non-disaggregated instance: 0 of 6,144 generated tokens off the argmax (> 0.5 nats) at concurrency 1 and 8. Exact-match differences (20 and 15 of 48) are at the level of the non-disaggregated instance against itself at different batch sizes (18 of 48). - **Failures** (240 requests, QPS 2, 1024-token prompts, 256 output tokens): - kill one of two decode instances: 240/240 complete, 9 resumed, all by re-pulling held KV (0 extra prefills), 0 off argmax, longest kill-to-next-token stall 0.63 s (3 runs, same outcome); - 2P2D, kill one decode and one prefill: 240/240, 11 resumes (11 re-pulls), 0 off argmax; - prefill killed while a transfer was pending (fault-injected, 3 runs): decode failed the load, router re-prefilled on the other prefill instance, all complete; - scaling a pool up and draining an instance under load: 240/240 complete.
Throughput/latency vs NixlConnector (1024-token prompts, 128 output tokens, same router and hosts) | connector | load | TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) | TPOT p50 / p99 (ms) | tok/s | |---|---|---|---|---| | ConnexConnector | QPS 1 | 354 / 537 | 31 / 33 | 128 | | NixlConnector | QPS 1 | 352 / 594 | 31 / 33 | 128 | | ConnexConnector | QPS 4 | 471 / 1003 | 36 / 38 | 459 | | NixlConnector | QPS 4 | 456 / 996 | 36 / 38 | 459 | | ConnexConnector | QPS 6 | 734 / 2090 | 38 / 40 | 694 | | NixlConnector | QPS 6 | 711 / 2018 | 38 / 40 | 694 | | ConnexConnector | 32 clients | 625 / 4939 | 38 / 38 | 639 | | NixlConnector | 32 clients | 573 / 4751 | 38 / 38 | 646 |
## Details Existing P/D connectors free the prefill blocks as soon as decode has read them, so once decoding starts the prompt KV exists in one place. If the decode instance dies (crash, preemption, spot scale-down), every in-flight request must be prefilled again or errors out. ConnexConnector makes the prefill-side copy a hold: a lease named by a transfer id, renewed by every pull, released by the decode instance when the request finishes or dropped after `retain_s` (default 60 s). `release: after_pull` frees blocks after the first read like other connectors. To resume, a router resends the same `kv_transfer_params` with the prompt plus the k generated tokens; the new decode instance async-loads `remote_num_tokens` and computes the k tokens locally. Instances can register their P/D role with the Connex front-router so instances can be added or removed at run time. Request flow: 1. Prefill instance (`kv_producer`) runs the prompt; on finish the scheduler keeps the blocks and returns `transfer_id`, `remote_ctrl`, `remote_num_tokens`. 2. Decode instance (`kv_consumer`) schedules the request as `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and pulls the blocks with one-sided reads. 3. Decode generates; on finish it sends a release, and the prefill worker reports the transfer done so the blocks are freed. 4. If decode dies before step 3, the router resends to another decode instance, which repeats step 2 against the still-held blocks. Changes: `v1/connex_connector.py` (lazy re-export with install hint), registration in `factory.py`, `docs/features/connex_connector_usage.md` plus an entry in `disagg_prefill.md`, and scheduler-level tests through the real `Scheduler`. Limitations: full-attention KV only; equal TP and block size on both sides. Developed with AI coding assistance; all changes were reviewed and tested by the author. ---

@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+# ConnexConnector Usage Guide
+
+`ConnexConnector` moves KV cache blocks from prefill to decode instances with
+[Connex](https://github.com/HeterInfra/connex), a communication library whose
+endpoints keep a stable logical identity while instances join, leave and fail.
+The connector itself is provided by the `connex-ai` package; vLLM only
+registers it.
+
+What it adds over a plain P/D transfer:
+
+- **Pull with a renewable hold.** The decode instance reads the prompt KV with
+  one-sided RDMA reads (connex-rs over UCX with GPUDirect RDMA, or Mooncake
+  Transfer Engine). The prefill instance keeps the blocks under a transfer id
+  until the decode instance releases them (or a lease expires), so if the
+  decode instance fails mid-generation, the request can be resumed on another
+  decode instance that pulls the same KV again instead of re-running prefill.
+  This reuse needs a resume that extends the original prompt token for token:
+  the Connex PD router does that for `/v1/completions` requests (token-ID
+  resume, the default). Chat requests, and completions resumed from text
+  (`--no-token-ids`), are resumed from text and run prefill again once tokens
+  have been emitted, even while the hold exists.
+- **Failure reporting per request.** A prefill instance that dies during a
+  transfer fails only the affected requests (load errors, handled by
+  `kv_load_failure_policy`), detected within milliseconds by connex-rs.
+- **Pool membership.** Instances can register their role in a Connex
+  front-router, which the Connex PD router (`connex.serving.pd_router`) uses
+  to add and remove prefill and decode instances at run time.
+
+## Installation
+
+```bash
+pip install "connex-ai[rs]"        # connex-rs data plane (RDMA hosts)
+# or
+pip install "connex-ai[mooncake]"  # Mooncake Transfer Engine data plane
+```
+
+## Usage
+
+Prefill instance (the two instances must use different GPUs: the decode
+instance refuses to pull from a prefill instance on its own GPU, and two
+instances on one GPU may also run out of memory):
+
+```bash
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B --port 8100 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"ConnexConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"ctrl_port":17100}}'
+```
+
+Decode instance:
+
+```bash
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 vllm serve meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B --port 8200 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"ConnexConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"}'
+```
+
+Router (follows the same `kv_transfer_params` protocol as the NIXL proxy
+example: prefill with `do_remote_decode`, then decode with the returned
+parameters; it also resumes requests whose decode instance fails):
+
+```bash
+python -m connex.serving.pd_router --port 8000 \
+    --prefill http://127.0.0.1:8100 --decode http://127.0.0.1:8200
+```
+
+## Configuration
+
+`kv_connector_extra_config` keys:
+
+| key | default | meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `backend` | unset | `connex-rs` or `mooncake`; leave unset to pick one automatically (connex-rs on RDMA hosts, else Mooncake) |
+| `host` | `VLLM_HOST_IP` | address peers use to reach this instance |
+| `ctrl_port` | `kv_port` | KV control port; TP rank `r` uses `ctrl_port + r` |
+| `retain_s` | `60` | prefill hold lease, renewed by every pull |
+| `release` | `on_finish` | `after_pull` frees prefill blocks right after the first pull |
+| `front_router`, `http_url`, `replica` | unset | register this instance in a Connex front-router |
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Full-attention models; prefill and decode must use the same tensor-parallel
+  size and block size (rank `r` pulls from rank `r`).
+- No hybrid (Mamba / sliding-window) KV groups and no pipeline parallelism
+  inside an instance yet.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Scheduler-level hand-off of ConnexConnector (requires connex-ai)."""
+
+import pytest
+
+pytest.importorskip("connex.adapters.vllm.pd_connector")
+
+from vllm.v1.request import RequestStatus  # noqa: E402
+
+from .utils import (  # noqa: E402
+    create_model_runner_output,
+    create_request,
+    create_scheduler,
+    create_vllm_config,
+)
+
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+PARAMS = {
+    "remote_ctrl": "10.0.0.1:17100",
+    "remote_engine_id": "prefill-0",
+    "remote_tp_size": 1,
+}
+
+
+def _scheduler(kv_role):
+    return create_scheduler(
+        create_vllm_config(
+            kv_connector="ConnexConnector",
+            kv_role=kv_role,
+            block_size=BLOCK_SIZE,
+            kv_connector_extra_config={"host": "10.0.0.1", "ctrl_port": 17100},
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def test_prefill_holds_blocks_until_released():
+    """The prefill keeps the blocks after the request finishes and frees
+    them only once the worker reports the transfer as done."""
+    scheduler = _scheduler("kv_producer")
+    req = create_request(num_tokens=3 * BLOCK_SIZE, do_remote_decode=True)
+    req.kv_transfer_params["transfer_id"] = "T"
+    scheduler.add_request(req)
+
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    meta = out.kv_connector_metadata
+    assert meta.holds == []
+    eco = scheduler.update_from_output(out, create_model_runner_output([req]))
+    params = eco[0].outputs[0].kv_transfer_params
+    assert params["do_remote_prefill"] and params["transfer_id"] == "T"
+    assert params["remote_ctrl"] == "10.0.0.1:17100"
+    assert params["remote_num_tokens"] == 3 * BLOCK_SIZE
+
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    (hold,) = out.kv_connector_metadata.holds
+    assert hold[:2] == (req.request_id, "T") and len(hold[2]) == 3
+    assert req.request_id in scheduler.requests  # blocks not freed yet
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        out, create_model_runner_output([], finished_sending={req.request_id})
+    )
+    assert req.request_id not in scheduler.requests
+
+
+def test_decode_loads_prompt_asynchronously_then_releases():
+    scheduler = _scheduler("kv_consumer")
+    req = create_request(num_tokens=2 * BLOCK_SIZE + 3, do_remote_prefill=True)
+    req.kv_transfer_params = {
+        "do_remote_prefill": True,
+        "transfer_id": "T",
+        **PARAMS,
+        "remote_num_tokens": 2 * BLOCK_SIZE + 3,
+    }
+    scheduler.add_request(req)
+
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    (pull,) = out.kv_connector_metadata.pulls
+    assert pull.transfer_id == "T" and pull.first_block == 0
+    assert len(pull.local_blocks) == 3
+    assert req.status == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
+
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        out, create_model_runner_output([], finished_recving={req.request_id})
+    )
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert req.status == RequestStatus.RUNNING
+
+    scheduler.finish_requests(req.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED)
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert out.kv_connector_metadata.releases == [("10.0.0.1:17100", "T", 1)]
+
+
+def test_resume_with_locally_cached_remote_prefix_runs_without_load():
+    """A resumed request whose remote prefix is already in the local prefix
+    cache loads nothing: it is scheduled RUNNING right away, and the pull it
+    still sends (to acquire the prefill hold) is acquire-only, so the worker
+    never reports it in finished_recving (which the scheduler only accepts
+    for waiting or finished requests)."""
+    from connex.adapters.vllm.pd_connector import _Pull
+
+    if "report" not in _Pull.__dataclass_fields__:
+        pytest.skip("connex-ai without acquire-only pulls")
+    scheduler = _scheduler("kv_consumer")
+    prefix = 2 * BLOCK_SIZE
+
+    # Populate the local prefix cache with the prompt's first two blocks.
+    warm = create_request(num_tokens=prefix + 1, common_prefix_len=prefix)
+    scheduler.add_request(warm)
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    scheduler.update_from_output(out, create_model_runner_output([warm]))
+    scheduler.finish_requests(warm.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_STOPPED)
+
+    # Resume: prompt + generated tokens, remote KV covers the cached prefix.
+    req = create_request(num_tokens=prefix + 5, common_prefix_len=prefix)
+    req.kv_transfer_params = {
+        "do_remote_prefill": True,
+        "transfer_id": "T",
+        **PARAMS,
+        "remote_num_tokens": prefix,
+    }
+    scheduler.add_request(req)
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert req.status == RequestStatus.RUNNING
+    assert out.num_scheduled_tokens[req.request_id] == 5  # prefix hit locally
+    (pull,) = out.kv_connector_metadata.pulls
+    assert pull.local_blocks == [] and pull.report is False
+
+    # The step completes with no receive report, and the request keeps running.
+    scheduler.update_from_output(out, create_model_runner_output([req]))
+    out = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert req.status == RequestStatus.RUNNING
+    assert out.kv_connector_metadata.pulls == []

+"""ConnexConnector: P/D disaggregation over Connex.
+
+The implementation lives in the ``connex-ai`` package
+(``connex.adapters.vllm.pd_connector``). It pulls KV blocks from the prefill
+instance with one-sided reads (connex-rs over UCX with GPUDirect RDMA, or
+Mooncake Transfer Engine) and keeps them on the prefill instance as a
+renewable hold until the decode instance releases them, so a request whose
+decode instance fails can be resumed on another decode instance without a
+second prefill. See docs/features/connex_connector_usage.md.
+"""
+
+try:
+    from connex.adapters.vllm.pd_connector import (
+        ConnexConnector,
+        ConnexConnectorMetadata,
+    )
+except ImportError as e:
+    raise ImportError(
+        "ConnexConnector requires the connex-ai package: "
+        "pip install 'connex-ai[rs]' (connex-rs data plane) or "
+        "'connex-ai[mooncake]' (Mooncake Transfer Engine)."
+    ) from e
+
+__all__ = ["ConnexConnector", "ConnexConnectorMetadata"]

inline_comments.body: The delegated adapter can crash the scheduler when a resumed request already has the remote prefix cached locally (e.g. 32 cached tokens, `remote_num_tokens=32`, and a longer resumed prompt). It returns `(0, False)` but still queues an empty pull in `update_state_after_alloc`, then reports its completion through `finished_recving`. The request is RUNNING, so `Scheduler._update_from_kv_xfer_finished` hits its finished-status assertion. Please fix the adapter to suppress receive completions for acquire-only pulls before exposing it here, and add a scheduler regression for this case.

Cross-process KV loads therefore fail. Document automatic selection as leaving this key unset, rather than listing `auto` as a supported explicit value.

inline_comments.body: Please qualify the no-reprefill recovery claim by API and resume mode. In Connex's `PDResumer.build()`, a retry after tokens have been emitted discards the saved KV parameters unless token-ID resume is active on a non-chat request, so chat and text-based resume run prefill again even while the hold exists. Document this restriction for users relying on KV reuse during failover.

inline_comments.body: The router example uses loopback addresses, but these two server commands select the same default GPU when run on one host. The connex-rs data plane explicitly rejects transfers when prefill and decode share a GPU, so this quickstart cannot transfer KV as written (and the second server may run out of memory first). Assign distinct GPUs to the two roles, for example GPU 0 for prefill and GPU 1 for decode.

+# ConnexConnector Usage Guide
+
+`ConnexConnector` moves KV cache blocks from prefill to decode instances with
+[Connex](https://github.com/HeterInfra/connex), a communication library whose
+endpoints keep a stable logical identity while instances join, leave and fail.
+The connector itself is provided by the `connex-ai` package; vLLM only
+registers it.
+
+What it adds over a plain P/D transfer:
+
+- **Pull with a renewable hold.** The decode instance reads the prompt KV with
+  one-sided RDMA reads (connex-rs over UCX with GPUDirect RDMA, or Mooncake
+  Transfer Engine). The prefill instance keeps the blocks under a transfer id
+  until the decode instance releases them (or a lease expires), so if the
+  decode instance fails mid-generation, the request can be resumed on another
+  decode instance that pulls the same KV again instead of re-running prefill.
+- **Failure reporting per request.** A prefill instance that dies during a
+  transfer fails only the affected requests (load errors, handled by
+  `kv_load_failure_policy`), detected within milliseconds by connex-rs.
+- **Pool membership.** Instances can register their role in a Connex
+  front-router, which the Connex PD router (`connex.serving.pd_router`) uses
+  to add and remove prefill and decode instances at run time.
+
+## Installation
+
+```bash
+pip install "connex-ai[rs]"        # connex-rs data plane (RDMA hosts)
+# or
+pip install "connex-ai[mooncake]"  # Mooncake Transfer Engine data plane
+```
+
+## Usage
+
+Prefill instance:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B --port 8100 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"ConnexConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"ctrl_port":17100}}'
+```
+
+Decode instance:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B --port 8200 \
+    --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"ConnexConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"}'
+```
+
+Router (follows the same `kv_transfer_params` protocol as the NIXL proxy
+example: prefill with `do_remote_decode`, then decode with the returned
+parameters; it also resumes requests whose decode instance fails):
+
+```bash
+python -m connex.serving.pd_router --port 8000 \
+    --prefill http://127.0.0.1:8100 --decode http://127.0.0.1:8200
+```
+
+## Configuration
+
+`kv_connector_extra_config` keys:
+
+| key | default | meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `backend` | `auto` | `connex-rs`, `mooncake` or `auto` |
